reader.requirement: The three entries with no true concept of level take the special level-numbers: 66 for a RENAMES regrouping entry, 77 for a noncontiguous working-storage or linkage item that is neither subordinate nor subdivided, 88 for a condition-name on the values of its conditional variable; the compiler must give each that meaning and refuse a special level used otherwise (77 in a record area, 77 subdivided or unnamed, 66 without RENAMES, 88 without a VALUE clause).
reader.edition-search: grep Edition/DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry/DialectBehavior in LevelNumberPass.cs (its own remarks state the level sets are not edition-gated) and in DataBinder.BindEntries' 66/77/88 arms: none. The LOCAL-STORAGE section and the 88 WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase are refused at 85 by their own construct gates, not on this path
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the 66/77/88 meanings and refusals are one code path at every edition; only the sections a 77 can sit in differ (85 has no LOCAL-STORAGE, refused by the section gate)

reader.notes: BindEntries binds 88 as a condition on the last described entry, 66 as an alias on the open record, and treats 77 as a root (nest level 1) so a following 02-49 opens no record and is refused. LevelNumberPass refuses the special numbers by section and by entry format before binding.

refuter.evidence: Probes refute-1985-187/lvok, lvr1-lvr4, lvr6-lvr9 (--std 85): accepted 66 after the record, 77 after an 01, 77 USAGE INDEX with no PICTURE, 88 under a 77; refused a 05 after the record's 66 (COBOL2740), an 88 under a 66 (COBOL1976, §1985:VI.5.3.4 GR2b), a 77 with neither PICTURE nor USAGE INDEX (COBOL0881), a 66 after a 77 or renaming a 77 or the 01 (COBOL2740), a 66 renaming an 88 (COBOL1655). SIBLING DEFECT, outside this rule: lvr7b.cob (runs/lvr7b-001) '66 X1 RENAMES A1 THRU A2. 66 X2 RENAMES X1.' compiles and prints X2 [ABCD] at --std 85, while --std 2023 refuses it (COBOL1655). §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR4: 'A 66 level entry cannot rename another 66 level entry' (cite.py OK). Cause (a): since PB5165 the 85 arm of DataBinder.RegionClauseCandidates searches the whole scope (QualifiedCandidates), which finds the level-66 alias; IsWithinRegion passes it and ResolveRedefinesPass.ScreenRenamesOperand tests only levels 1 and 77, its comment assuming 66 is unreachable. That is a RENAMES syntax-rule defect (under-rejects, cause a), not a failure of GR3's assignment of the special levels; no kb/Work note found (grep 'renam* a 66' / PB5165 notes). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.2.1 GR3  (4.3.2.1 Level-Numbers)  the text is in GR3'; 'OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR4  (5.11.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4'.
